references.text: Moses was on the mountain for forty days and forty nights without eating or drinking, while he received the tablets of the law again.
Moses reminds the people that he was on the mountain for forty days and forty nights when he received the stone tablets.
Moses describes how he fell down before the Lord for forty days and forty nights because of the people's sin.
Moses was once more on the mountain for forty days and forty nights when he received the new stone tablets.
Elijah went for forty days and forty nights to God's mountain Horeb, echoing Moses' stay on the mountain.
Jesus fasted for forty days and forty nights in the wilderness, as a parallel to Moses' time on the mountain.
The Lord came to Moses in a thick cloud on Mount Sinai, setting the stage for Moses' entry into the cloud.
The cloud covered the mountain for six days before the Lord called Moses into the cloud on the seventh day.
Stephen refers to Moses who was on Mount Sinai and received living words from the angel.
A chronological connection where the verses show the transition from God's call to Moses' entry into the divine presence on the mountain.
Complementary movements illustrating ritual purity (descent) and divine entry (ascent) in the covenant process.
Parallel action (ascending with the tablets) that underscores the theme of God's grace in restoring the covenant after the people broke it.
Connects the hidden meeting in the cloud (24) with the revealed communication outside (34), illustrating the boundary between divine holiness and public proclamation.
